messages:
alex: Hey folks — heads up I'm planning to work remotely from Recife, Brazil for ~3 months (mid-Jun to mid-Sep) while my partner sorts a visa. Quick Qs: payroll implications, WFH stipend proration, shipping company laptop/peripherals, and any tax nexus risk for Redwood? Do I need an approval workflow?

jordan-peopleops: Congrats! Need a few details but short answers: benefits generally continue, payroll is the tricky part (we don't have Brazil payroll), stipend can be prorated. We'll need manager sign-off + short-term remote addendum.

maria-payroll: We don't operate payroll in Brazil right now. For stays <=90 days we can typically keep you on US payroll but we require: signed short-term remote addendum, return travel evidence, and your manager's approval. WFH stipend is prorated monthly and paid in USD to your existing direct deposit. Equipment: shipping company laptops overseas is discouraged because of customs/duty and asset tracking. Peripherals we can either reimburse receipts or ship at your cost. Fill this form: https://intranet.redwood/forms/short-term-remote and attach dates + itinerary.

legal-bot: Legal note: Brazil has specific rules that can create permanent establishment risk depending on activity and client interactions. 90 days is usually a safe threshold but not a guarantee. We'll loop in external counsel to confirm. Please avoid signing any contracts or doing local hiring while abroad.

lee: Benefits check — international emergency travel medical covers some countries but not all. Ping benefits@ with exact dates so we can confirm coverage. Also make sure VPN + company-approved firewall configs are in place.

alex: Thanks — good to know. A couple micro Qs: 1) Will stipend show as USD on paystub? 2) If I buy a local SIM do I need expense approval?

maria-payroll: 1) Yes, stipend will appear as USD on your US paystub. 2) Local SIM is reimbursable under travel/telecom up to policy limits — save receipts and submit via Expensify with code "Remote-Travel".

jordan-peopleops: Manager approval needed. @sam can you confirm coverage for overlap hours and that team is ok with asynchronous work? :thumbsup:

sam: I approve, as long as Alex keeps at least 3 hours overlap with PST core hours and we have the return date documented. Please add timeline to the team calendar.

maria-payroll: Next steps from payroll/legal side: 
```
1) Alex submits short-term remote form + dates
2) Manager signs off in the form
3) People Ops issues short-term remote addendum to sign
4) Payroll confirms paystub/stipend handling
5) Legal does quick counsel check (~3-5 business days)
```
We'll aim to complete in 7-10 business days once we have the form.

legal-bot: Escalating to counsel now. If counsel flags any PE concerns we'll update and may request to shorten the stay or change work scope.

alex: Great — I'll fill the form today and post dates. Appreciate fast turnaround! :pray:

jordan-peopleops: Thanks Alex — ping us once submitted and we'll track the ticket.
